title: U.S. 10-year Treasury yield crosses 5%, raising software-IPO valuation risk
summary: The benchmark long-term yield crossed a valuation-sensitive threshold, increasing the discount rate for long-duration software cash flows and making premium private-company multiples harder to sustain. The downgrade applies the lowest end of the repository's valuation-compression rule without changing Kong's operating assessment or model defaults.
confirmed: Reuters reported that the benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury yield rose above 5% on September 14, 2026, its highest level since October 2023, and was last at 5.01% in the cited report.
Reuters attributed the move to higher-for-longer rate expectations, renewed inflation concerns after an oil-price jump, heavy debt issuance, and fiscal-risk premiums.
Kong's press room still lists the September 9 Forrester announcement as its latest release, and its blog still lists the September 10 Straiker integration as its latest post.
uncertain: A one-day yield threshold may reverse; it does not prove that Kong's eventual IPO window will be closed or establish the revenue multiple available when Kong prices an offering.
No new Kong ARR, revenue growth, gross margin, free-cash-flow margin, retention, customer concentration, fully diluted share count, IPO filing, or timetable was disclosed.
Private-market pages displayed algorithmic Kong price estimates but did not establish a verified arm's-length transaction or executable market price.
